subject: radiology
title: CT Head in Trauma: Extradural and Subdural Haematomas

steps.title: Biconvex extradural collection
steps.tx: **Extradural haematoma** collects between skull and dura as a biconvex, lens shaped high density mass that respects suture lines where dura is tacked down but crosses the midline freely. The pictured CT anatomy set shows that lens shape over the temporal region, classic after a fracture tears the middle meningeal artery. A lucid interval between injury and deterioration is the clinical story examiners attach to this shape.
steps.say: Extradural haematoma collects between skull and dura as a biconvex lens shaped mass that respects suture lines but crosses the midline. The pictured CT shows that lens over the temporal region, classic after a fracture tears the middle meningeal artery. A lucid interval is the story examiners attach.

vis.caption: Biconvex extradural haematoma on CT with related anatomy. Illustration: StewardMD.

steps.title: Crescentic subdural collection
steps.tx: **Subdural haematoma** spreads between dura and arachnoid as a crescent that crosses suture lines but stops at the falx and tentorium, so it never crosses the midline. The pictured chronic subdural shows the crescent hugging the hemisphere in an older patient after minor trauma tore bridging veins. Acute subdural density is bright like extradural, so shape and suture behaviour, not brightness, separate the two at first look.
steps.say: Subdural haematoma spreads between dura and arachnoid as a crescent crossing suture lines but stopping at the falx, so it never crosses the midline. The pictured chronic subdural hugs the hemisphere after bridging vein tears. Shape and suture behaviour, not brightness, separate it from extradural blood.

vis.alt: CT showing crescentic chronic subdural haematoma over a cerebral hemisphere.
vis.caption: Crescentic chronic subdural haematoma on CT. Illustration: StewardMD.

steps.title: Density dates the bleed
steps.tx: **Haematoma density** fades on a timetable: acute blood is hyperdense at 50 to 80 Hounsfield units for about the first three days, turns isodense with cortex between one and three weeks, then hypodense like fluid after three weeks. The isodense phase is the trap, betrayed only by sulci that vanish, grey white junction displaced inward and a ventricle squeezed on the same side.
steps.say: Haematoma density fades on a timetable: acute blood is bright for about three days, turns isodense with cortex between one and three weeks, then dark like fluid. The isodense phase betrays itself only by vanished sulci, displaced grey white junction and a squeezed ventricle.

steps.title: Midline shift and herniation
steps.tx: **Midline shift** is measured at the septum pellucidum or pineal gland, and shift over 5 mm with a deteriorating patient drives urgent neurosurgical discussion. Uncal herniation pushes the medial temporal lobe over the tentorium, effacing the ambient cistern and compressing the third nerve to blow the pupil. Subfalcine shift slides the cingulate under the falx, and tonsillar descent through the foramen magnum is the final, often fatal, event.
steps.say: Midline shift is measured at the septum pellucidum, and shift over five millimetres with deterioration drives urgent neurosurgical discussion. Uncal herniation effaces the ambient cistern and blows the pupil. Subfalcine shift slides the cingulate under the falx, and tonsillar descent is the final event.

steps.title: Fractures and the pterion
steps.tx: **Pterion fracture** matters because the middle meningeal artery grooves the bone exactly there, four centimetres above the zygomatic arch midpoint region. A fracture line crossing the arterial groove beside an extradural lens confirms the bleeding source. Depressed fractures deeper than the skull table thickness, open fractures and fractures over a venous sinus each change management toward theatre, antibiotics or extreme elevation caution respectively.
steps.say: Pterion fracture matters because the middle meningeal artery grooves the bone exactly there. A fracture crossing the arterial groove beside an extradural lens confirms the source. Depressed fractures deeper than the skull table, open fractures and fractures over a venous sinus each change management toward theatre or caution.

steps.title: Swirl sign means active bleeding
steps.tx: **Swirl sign** mixes low density fresh unclotted blood inside a brighter clotted haematoma, marking active or recent bleeding and a collection likely to expand. It upgrades urgency in both extradural and subdural bleeds and appears in spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage too. Anticoagulant or antiplatelet use, a wide pupil and falling consciousness beside a swirl sign collection should already have neurosurgery and reversal agents moving before the formal report lands.
steps.say: Swirl sign mixes low density fresh blood inside brighter clot, marking active bleeding and a collection likely to expand. It upgrades urgency in extradural and subdural bleeds alike. Anticoagulant use, a wide pupil and falling consciousness beside it should move neurosurgery and reversal before the report lands.

steps.title: Diffuse injury without a collection
steps.tx: **Diffuse axonal injury** shears white matter at the grey white junction, corpus callosum and dorsolateral brainstem, often with a near normal CT apart from tiny haemorrhagic dots. MRI with susceptibility sequences is far more sensitive and grades depth of lesions, brainstem involvement carrying the worst prognosis. A patient in coma with a clean CT after high speed trauma has diffuse injury until MRI proves otherwise, never a reassuring scan.
steps.say: Diffuse axonal injury shears white matter at the grey white junction, corpus callosum and brainstem, often with a near normal CT apart from tiny dots. MRI is far more sensitive, and brainstem lesions carry the worst prognosis. Coma with a clean CT after high speed trauma means diffuse injury until proven otherwise.

steps.title: Contusions blossom and contrecoup
steps.tx: **Cerebral contusions** bruise the inferior frontal and anterior temporal poles where brain scrapes over skull base ridges, appearing as mixed density haemorrhagic patches that blossom over 24 to 48 hours. Contrecoup bruising sits opposite the impact point, coup beneath it. Repeat CT catches blossoming before herniation, which is why a talking patient with frontal contusions and anticoagulant use earns observation rather than discharge.
steps.say: Cerebral contusions bruise the inferior frontal and anterior temporal poles where brain scrapes over skull base ridges, blossoming over twenty four to forty eight hours. Contrecoup bruising sits opposite the impact. Repeat CT catches blossoming before herniation, so anticoagulated patients with frontal contusions earn observation.
